📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that kia’s EV lineup covers just about every size and price point, but it believes one thing is still missing: a truly cheap electric car. That’s about to change in 2027, when Kia plans to unveil a fresh EV that could start at around $22,000 to $24,000.

It’s been 40 years since Kia introduced its first electric vehicle, the Besta EV, created so runners in the 1986 Asian Games wouldn’t have to breathe toxic fumes from the broadcast vehicle.

Kia has come a long way since the Besta EV hit the road, now offering a complete lineup of electric vehicles, from compact SUVs and hatchbacks to vans and three-row SUVs.

In Europe and the UK, Kia’s electric lineup consists of the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van, but the Korean automaker isn’t done yet.

“With no intention of resting on its laurels,” Kia said, the brand aims to complete development of its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) by the end of 2027, an all-new B-segment EV hatchback.

It didn’t offer any other details on the upcoming EV, but Ted Lee, Kia’s executive vice president and head of global operations, told Auto Express that Kia and Hyundai are co-developing a latest dedicated EV architecture for an upcoming pair of entry-level electric cars.

Expected to arrive as the Hyundai IONIQ 1 and Kia EV1, the newly introduced EVs will compete with other entry-level electric cars like the Renault Twingo, which starts at about €20,000.

Recent findings suggest that lee said the EV1’s price will be highly competitive not just with other entry-level EVs, but also with small gas-powered cars, with prices expected to start in the €20,000 to €22,000 range, or about $22,000 to $24,000. And that’s without government incentives.

The EV2 starts at just €26,600 ($29,500) in Germany and other European markets as Kia’s current entry-level EV, so the price range would make sense.

While it will be Kia’s cheapest EV, Lee promised it would not cut corners in quality, design, or features.

According to recent reports, as its first SDV, the EV1 will feature Kia and Hyundai Motor’s latest-generation tech and software. Kia noted the electric SDV will offer Level 2+ autonomous driving on highways. In 2029, Kia intends to expand to Level 2++, enabling it to operate in cities.

The latest EV will also use Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), the Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.

What will the EV1 look like? According to Auto Express, the entry-level EV will look a bit sportier and less boxy than the EV2 SUV. It could draw inspiration from the Vision Meta Turismo concept.

Industry observers note that it also apparently won’t be based on the Picanto, Kia’s smallest gas-powered car. The Kia EV1 is expected to bring a unique style to the family.

It has been revealed that this is good to see and makes sense, especially in Europe. I don't think Kia can go wrong making vehicles at so many different price points. It allows them to reach different segments and almost literally have something for almost everyone.

While all of Kia’s current EVs feature its ccNC infotainment system with dual 12.3″ instrument display and infotainment screens, plus a 5″ climate control panel, the EV1 could bring a simpler setup.

Like its other electric models, the EV1 is expected to receive the GT treatment. However, as an entry-level model, it may not use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup like the others.

Sources indicate that will Kia bring the EV1 to the US? Don’t get your hopes up. Kia has previously said the B-segment hatchback is designed for Europe. It could even be built alongside the EV2 at Kia’s plant in Slovakia.

It has been revealed that the good news? The EV3, Kia’s compact electric SUV, is now on sale in the US, starting at just $29,890.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of newly introduced fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

Recent findings suggest that the list of notes for patch 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

It has been revealed that this fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an concern whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

Sources indicate that the game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

According to recent reports, 1.4.0 also fixes an especially nasty exploit that allowed players to bring up their weapons much faster than normal by quickly swapping to the quick use menu. There’s a range of smaller fixes for lighting and texture bugs here, too, and you can read all about it in the full change log below:.

According to recent reports, for enthusiasts, tire shopping is an upgrade, not a chore. While the casual driver might treat new tires like regular maintenance, anyone who cares about vehicle dynamics knows that what meets the road defines how a truck or SUV rides, tracks, and stops. It is the single most transformative upgrade you can make to your vehicle. For more than 110 years, Cooper tires have catered to drivers who look past the showroom floor and seek out products that overdeliver on performance, capability, and long-term durability.

Recent findings suggest that and that level of purpose-built engineering is more vital than ever. As vehicles grow heavier and more capable, tires need to do more than simply roll down an interstate. They have to withstand heavy payload demands, sudden weather changes, and unpredictable pavement. Cooper tires are built to that benchmark. Rooted in American engineering and real-world development, Cooper tires are built to an uncompromising standard that live up to their promises. From the rock-crawling STT Pro to the severe-snow-designated Stronghold AT, the Discoverer® family has earned its reputation through real-world testing from Alaskan ice to jagged mountain trails.

The fresh Cooper Discoverer® HT adapts that rugged all-terrain lineage for long-distance highway cruising, matching heavy-duty capability with quiet, refined composure. While it retains the structural durability to wander down a gravel trail with a trailer in tow, its core mission is maximizing comfort and control across hundreds of miles of open road.

In a recent development, where many highway tires trade load capability for a soft ride, the Discoverer® HT is engineered to handle both. Straight, reinforced sidewalls provide the structural foundation needed to maintain an optimal contact patch under load. Whether the vehicle is running light or carrying family, gear, and tongue weight, the tire resists deformation, ensuring consistent steering response and predictable roadholding grip in any condition. It’s engineered for drivers whose tires have to hold their own—providing a dependable, hard-working partner that won’t fold when the truck or SUV is pushed to its limit.

In a recent development, cooper tires also tackle truck and SUV tire performance, with advanced features. Its proprietary 3-D Micro-Gauge Siping incorporates interlocking zig-zag sipes inside the tread blocks. Under heavy braking, sharp turns, or loaded acceleration, these interlocking sipes lock together to stiffen the tread block, to help support responsiveness. Crucially, these sipes run deep into the tread rubber, ensuring that gripping edges are still present to help with traction. That structural integrity backs up an exceptional UTQG treadwear rating of 720 and a 70,000-mile limited treadwear warranty on passenger fitments.

This is the tire for drivers who expect their trucks or suvs to show up for the long haul. Whether that means towing a camper into the backcountry, handling moving-day payloads, or eating up cross-country interstate miles in quiet comfort, the mission remains the same: a single set of tires that balances real-world traction, refined manners, and hard-working capability.

To fit that wide spectrum of work, Cooper offers the Discoverer® HT across 19 passenger sizes covering 16- to 22-inch wheels (with section widths from 245 to 285 mm), alongside 16 light-truck (LT) options engineered with deeper tread grooves and higher load ratings. Backed by a 45-day satisfaction guarantee and over a century of research and development, the Discoverer® HT delivers what Cooper has always stood for: the quiet confidence that the job was done right.

#63835. Life in Isolation: Are We Living in a Human Zoo?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (625 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Life in Isolation: Are We Living in a Human Zoo?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • According to recent reports, in Stolen Focus, Johann Hari explores the distress of captive animals through veterinary behaviorist Nicholas Dodman's description of "frustrated biological objectives": innate needs that remain active even when circumstances prevent their expression.
  • Sources indicate that let’s consider if zoochosis could apply to human beings too: could some of our depression and anxiety be less about defective individuals and more about the increasingly unnatural environments we live in?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

According to recent reports, in Stolen Focus, Johann Hari explores the distress of captive animals through veterinary behaviorist Nicholas Dodman's description of "frustrated biological objectives": innate needs that remain active even when circumstances prevent their expression. Zoochosis describes abnormal behaviors observed in captive animals, including compulsive self-directed activity.

Sources indicate that let’s consider if zoochosis could apply to human beings too: could some of our depression and anxiety be less about defective individuals and more about the increasingly unnatural environments we live in? We recognize something is wrong when a tiger paces endlessly in a concrete enclosure. Yet when human beings experience restlessness, alienation, depression, or anxiety, we are remarkably quick to diagnose them. “I don’t know who discovered water but I doubt it was a fish,” mentioned Marshall McLuhan. Maybe it’s the water that surrounds us that’s toxic and not something inside of us?

Industry observers note that remote work, online shopping, food delivery, streaming entertainment, and virtual socializing have become increasingly normal since the pandemic. Many of these things are genuinely convenient and some have improved people's quality of life. But maybe our frictionless lives are not necessarily an upgrade to the human experience? Maybe we thrive when we have little victories like trips to the store, restaurants, gyms and other third spaces where we interact with others?

Recent findings suggest that we work on one screen, order necessities through another, socialize through messages, exercise in front of a monitor, and unwind by scrolling through videos of other people living lives that appear to be more interesting and exciting than our own. We can spend days on end interacting with two-dimensional representations of the world without actually being face-to-face with other people. Ever heard of pheromones?

We accumulate hundreds of online acquaintances without experiencing the vulnerability and authenticity that we need and crave. We communicate constantly while remaining profoundly lonely.

Humans evolved to move through complex physical terrains, not sit on couches with laptops on our laps. We need touching, exploring, smelling, creating, cooperating, taking risks, and belonging to communities in three dimensions, not two.

And being constantly available is not our friend. Neither is excessive optimization nor compulsive productivity. Having no time for friends, family, or contemplation should be seen as failure. We can no longer simply take a walk; we need to track our steps, monitor our heart rates, and demonstrate that we have accomplished something in contrast to “just walking.”.

So what if some of what we call individual psychopathology is really a response to collective conditions that frustrate fundamental human needs?

Recent findings suggest that psychology should examine not only what patients are thinking and feeling but also take into account the influences that are causing people to think and feel the way they do. We should ask questions such as, “Do they have true agency? Are they physically engaged with the world? Do they experience meaningful relationships, belonging, creativity, and contribution? Do they have opportunities to experience spontaneity, wonder, and delight?”.

Industry observers note that perhaps we need to reconsider the conditions under which we expect human beings to live, work, love, and flourish. That means examining not only individual choices but also workplaces, economic incentives, social institutions, and the technologies that increasingly mediate our experience of reality.

Helping people adapt to their circumstances is an important part of psychotherapy but our adaptation to COVID-lockdown reclusiveness may be more akin to zoochosis than we have hitherto believed.

Hari, J. (2022). "Stolen Focus: Why You Can't Pay Attention—and How to Think Deeply Again." Crown.

Industry observers note that in bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

For this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

It has been revealed that tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

#63829. If You Can't Do These 5 Things, Your Divorce Will Be Hellish

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1362 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

If You Can't Do These 5 Things, Your Divorce Will Be Hellish

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1362 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • According to recent reports, jared hated his soon-to-be ex, Ashley, more than words could say.
  • It has been revealed that nan never expected her marriage to end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

According to recent reports, jared hated his soon-to-be ex, Ashley, more than words could say. In his eyes, she'd used him for his money, cheated on him with his best friend, Miguel, and then dumped him like garbage. He was hurt, betrayed, and furious. Who wouldn't be?

It has been revealed that nan never expected her marriage to end. She'd always been anxious, but now the bottom had fallen out of her world. Had he ever loved her? Would the kids be traumatized? Would she lose the house—the one place she felt safe? Would she have enough money to live on? Could she end up homeless? Would she have a breakdown like her mother did?

Sean felt nothing when his husband left a note saying he'd moved out and wasn't coming back. He sat in front of the TV for days, barely eating or getting off the couch. Friends called, but he let everything go to voicemail. He was emotionally numb.

Although these reactions may seem extreme, they're not unusual after a sudden split or an ugly breakup. Normal, that is, in the beginning.

Divorce is one of the toughest transitions anyone will go through. Even under the best circumstances, it can destabilize your home, finances, parenting, friendships, and sense of identity.

Sources indicate that looking at divorce through Maslow's hierarchy of needs, many folks feel knocked down to the two lowest levels: basic survival and safety. The higher-functioning levels of love, esteem, and self-actualization take a back seat.

When you're dividing assets, potentially doubling your expenses, and perhaps splitting time with your kids, you're understandably more focused on getting through today than on what you might gain tomorrow.

And this is where your brain comes in.

In a recent development, the amygdala is a small structure deep within the brain that helps detect threats and trigger emotional responses. It's part of a larger system involved in our fight, flight, or freeze reactions.

Industry observers note that jared's rage, Nan's fear, and Sean's shutdown illustrate different responses to overwhelming stress. Clients have told me they feel like their substantial emotions mean they're "going crazy." I tell them they're probably not going crazy. They're being stretched emotionally, sometimes beyond anything they've experienced before.

Ideally, as the initial shock wears off, rage softens into anger, terror becomes manageable fear, and numbness begins to thaw. But not everyone moves out of survival mode easily—especially if the loss triggers previous unresolved losses or traumas.

Fortunately, another part of the brain can help: the prefrontal cortex.

Located just behind your forehead, it helps with reasoning, planning, impulse control, and thinking through actions and their consequences. It’s the part of the brain that asks, "Is this really a good idea?" “Should I say exactly what’s on my mind right now?”.

Sources indicate that under intense stress, these skills can become compromised. You're more likely to react impulsively, see things in black-and-white terms, and seek immediate relief, rather than consider long-term consequences.

The amygdala and prefrontal cortex work together, but when our threat-response system is on high alert, thoughtful decisions become harder.

Recent findings suggest that that's why people sometimes do things during divorce they'd never dream of doing otherwise. They send vicious texts, threaten to take the kids away, spend thousands fighting over possessions worth far less, or make financial decisions that hurt them more than their spouse.

These actions may feel justified in the moment. But there's a difference between reacting to pain and making decisions that serve you.

Just because your spouse sends an inflammatory text doesn't mean you have to answer immediately—or at all.

Your first impulse may be to defend yourself or fire back. Don't. Unless there's an emergency, give yourself time to settle down. Sometimes an hour is enough. Sometimes you need a day.

It has been revealed that 2. Distinguish immediate emotional discharge from long-term benefit.

There can be something satisfying about telling your spouse exactly what you think of them or making sure they don't "get away with" what they've done.

Industry observers note that but that satisfaction is usually short-lived. The consequences may not be.

Ask yourself: "Will this help me build the life I want after divorce, or am I just trying to feel better right now?".

Sources indicate that 3. Consider your children's needs without disregarding your own.

Industry observers note that some parents become so consumed with their hurt that they lose sight of what their children are experiencing. Others sacrifice their own well-being because they believe putting the kids first means putting themselves last.

According to recent reports, neither extreme is helpful. Children need stability and emotional safety. They also benefit from parents who take care of themselves.

It has been revealed that I've seen people spend more on attorney fees fighting over furniture than the furniture was worth. I know of one wealthier couple who spent thousands of dollars fighting over cleaning products (I couldn't make that up)!

At that point, it's clearly not about the item being fought over as much as it is about feeling wronged, wanting control, or needing to win.

Before digging in your heels, ask: "Will this matter five years from now?".

Some things absolutely are worth fighting for, including safety, your children's well-being, and financial security. But not every disagreement deserves a battle.

5. Be willing to compromise without abandoning yourself.

One of the hardest things about divorce is accepting that you probably won't get everything you want. In some cases, you'll feel like your spouse is getting more than they deserve. It can perpetuate, or even exacerbate, your pain.

It has been revealed that ask yourself if you really want to keep fighting, or do you want to be done so you can move on? That's not to suggest that you should surrender or let your spouse take advantage of you. It means recognizing that a workable resolution may be better for your long-term mental health than winning every argument.

Just a note about safety: When abuse, coercion, or intimidation is involved, safety and legal protection come first.

Industry observers note that you're not going to feel calm and rational every minute. Divorce hurts. Sometimes terribly. You're allowed to be angry, frightened, or devastated. The problem isn't having these feelings. It's what you do with them.

Here's how to engage your higher brain: Before taking action, ask yourself:.

"Am I trying to solve a problem, protect myself, or punish someone?".

Sometimes you're protecting yourself, and that's appropriate. Other times, you may realize you want your spouse to hurt as much as you do. That's human, too. But acting on that impulse rarely gets you where you want to go.

You may not control your spouse's behavior or how the divorce unfolds. But you can recognize when you're operating from fear, anger, or overwhelm.

It has been revealed that the goal isn't to divorce without feeling deeply. It's to make sure temporary emotions don't create permanent consequences.

It has been revealed that after all, divorce isn't the last chapter of your life. You still have to live with your decisions long after it's over. The intense feelings you feel are in your body, not theirs. How long do you want to live with those emotions hijacking your pleasure and taking away your power? Practice letting go daily. Join a support group. Get into individual therapy. Read helpful books. Meditate. Your power is in where you are headed, not where you've been. Keep moving forward.

#63828. Breaking: High Fat Diet Linked to Higher Colon Cancer Risk, Early Research Indicates

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1275 w)

Breaking: High Fat Diet Linked to Higher Colon Cancer Risk, Early Research Indicates

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1275 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a new study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.
  • The researchers from Arizona State University stated a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.
  • The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a new study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.

The researchers from Arizona State University stated a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.

The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.

The researchers published their findings on November 12 in the journal Stem Cell Reports.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers stated the study is vital because 1 in 25 people develop colon cancer in their lifetime. In the United States, that translates into about 108,000 upcoming cases of colon cancer every year. About 55,000 males and 55,000 females are expected to die from the disease in 2026.

Experts not involved in the study say the research provides valuable information, but they have reservations about the results, as the findings do not yet apply to humans.

“The findings provide a potential mechanism linking diet to intestinal cancer development, but we need to be cautious about translating these results to humans,” mentioned Dalia Perelman, MS, CDE, a research dietitian at Stanford University in California.

Sources indicate that “We already have evidence from human studies that obesity and certain dietary patterns, particularly those high in processed meats and low in fiber-rich foods, are associated with increased colorectal cancer risk,” Perelman told Healthline. “This study adds a potentially vital mechanism to investigate, but it does not establish that dietary fat itself increases colorectal cancer risk in humans.”.

Ketan Thanki, MD, a colorectal surgeon specializing in benign and malignant diseases of the colon, rectum, and anus at the MemorialCare Todd Cancer Institute at Long Beach Medical Center in California, shared similar views.

“This study provides a better understanding at the cellular level of how a high fat diet may contribute to colorectal cancer development,” Thanki told Healthline.

“Animal studies are an crucial starting point for understanding biological processes, but we must be cautious about directly applying their findings to humans,” he added. “Mice and humans share many cellular and biological mechanisms, which makes these studies valuable in identifying potential pathways involved in disease development. However, human diets, genetics, metabolism, and environmental exposures are more complex.”.

To reach their findings, the Arizona State researchers fed mice what the scientists described as a Western-style high fat diet for 6 months.

They then compared those results with those from mice given a low fat diet.

According to recent reports, the researchers said the mice on the high fat diet gained more weight than the mice on the low-fat diet. They also developed more intestinal stem cells, and those cells grew at a more rapid rate.

They added that mice genetically predisposed to intestinal cancer who were fed a high-fat diet developed more and larger tumors.

The researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may help explain their increased growth and survival.

They also pointed out that stem cell behavior returned to normal after high fat diet mice were switched to a low fat diet, although some DNA changes persisted. After four weeks, approximately 18% of these changes remained.

When mice were returned to a high fat diet, the researchers said their intestinal stem cells responded more quickly and strongly than those of mice exposed to the diet for the first time.

They concluded that the study suggests that maintaining a healthy, low fat diet may help regulate intestinal stem cell growth and reduce colon cancer risk.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, RD, president of KAK Consulting and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine in Ohio, wasn’t involved in the study but highlighted a particular aspect of the findings.

In a recent development, “What I found particularly interesting was that even after the mice returned to a low fat diet, some of the molecular changes persisted,” she told Healthline. “This raises questions about how our dietary patterns over time may influence long-term health.”.

Experts mentioned these newly introduced findings are interesting but noted numerous caveats.

According to recent reports, “One key takeaway is that dietary habits over time matter,” mentioned Thanki. “Even if someone has consumed a high fat diet for years, making changes now may still provide meaningful health benefits.”.

“I also think these findings are particularly key for children and adolescents, as establishing healthier dietary habits early in life may provide long-term benefits,” he added.

However, Thanki noted that not all fats are the same. “The health risks depend partly on the type of fat consumed, how much is consumed, and what foods make up the overall diet,” he noted.

“Diets consistently high in saturated fats, particularly those containing large amounts of processed meats, fried foods, and highly processed products, can contribute to obesity, elevated cholesterol, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction. These factors can also contribute to chronic inflammation and may increase the risk of certain cancers, including colorectal cancer,” Thanki continued.

Perelman stated the diet used in the study was extremely high in fat, providing 60% of calories from fat, primarily from lard.

“We know that the health effects of dietary fats differ depending on their sources and fatty acid composition, and we cannot assume that a diet rich in unsaturated fats from foods such as olive oil, nuts, and seeds would produce the same effects,” she noted.

Perelman added that the researchers primarily studied stem cells from the small intestine rather than the colon.

“Although these tissues share some biological characteristics, they have crucial differences, and we cannot assume that the same changes would occur in the colon,” she explained.

Finally, Perelman noted that “the mice consuming the high fat diet also gained weight, making it difficult to separate the effects of dietary fat itself from those associated with increased body fat and other metabolic changes.”.

Not all high fat foods are unhealthy. Some high fat foods that offer healthy benefits include:.

“The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to eliminate fat because our bodies need healthy fats for normal functioning,” said Thanki. “Instead, people should focus on reducing saturated and trans fats while incorporating healthier unsaturated fats in appropriate amounts.”.

Thanki had several dietary suggestions. Among them:.

Industry observers note that “Consistency matters more than perfection. Even modest dietary changes, maintained over time, can have meaningful health benefits,” Thanki said.

According to recent reports, perelman agreed. “The overall quality of the diet matters. Diets that are very high in fat may displace other foods and nutrients that have important health benefits,” she mentioned.

“For colorectal cancer specifically, higher intakes of dietary fiber and whole grains have consistently been associated with lower risk,” Perelman noted.

“Therefore, rather than focusing exclusively on reducing fat, it is key to consider the overall dietary pattern and whether it provides adequate amounts of fiber-rich plant foods and other beneficial nutrients.”.

It has been revealed that kirkpatrick agreed that the type of fat is what is important. “A Mediterranean-style diet that includes olive oil, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish can be relatively high in fat but is consistently associated with positive health outcomes,” she remarked.

“On the other hand, a diet high in saturated fat, processed meats, and ultra-processed foods may increase the risk of certain chronic diseases, particularly when it’s also low in fiber and other protective nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick also noted that many lifestyle habits contribute to a person’s overall health.

“Our health is influenced by so many factors beyond diet, including how we manage stress, our sleep habits, physical activity, genetics, and overall lifestyle,” she stated.

  • While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the latest documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the latest documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley noted in a recent announcement.

The somewhat upcoming United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our consumers have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

Recent findings suggest that the collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets users explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are at the moment available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

Recent findings suggest that correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alpitronic, the company that makes the DC fast chargers used by Ionna, Walmart, Mercedes-Benz, BP Pulse, and others, is building a upcoming factory in the United States that will boost output of its 400- and 1,000-kilowatt stalls.

The manufacturer’s newly introduced 173,315-square-foot facility, located in Fort Mill, South Carolina, will create 70 new jobs and will also act as a testing lab, repair center, logistics hub, and warehouse.

Alpitronic, which has its North American headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, and its global headquarters in Bolzano, Italy, mentioned it will invest $33.94 million in the new facility, with $200,000 coming from York County’s Coordinating Council for Economic Development in the form of a Set-Aside grant to assist with the costs of building improvements.

“North America is central to our next phase of growth, and investing in our manufacturing capabilities is key to supporting that expansion,” said Patrik Herrnegger, Alpitronic Americas CEO. “Our Fort Mill facility will put U.S. production under our direct control, bringing us closer to our customers and enabling us to serve them more efficiently. We thank South Carolina and York County for their partnership as we prepare to begin production in early 2027.”.

Back in 2024, the manufacturer worked with a third-party production partner to open its first local manufacturing facility in Wisconsin. Now, manufacturing has moved in-house, with Alpitronic wholly owning the production operation.

The new South Carolina plant will assemble HYC400 and HYC1000 stalls, Alpitronic noted. The HYC400 all-in-one dispensers can deliver up to 400 kW of power to a single connected electric vehicle without needing a separate power cabinet, and are the current charger of choice for Ionna and Walmart.

Sources indicate that the higher-powered HYC1000 system is composed of a 1,000-kW power cabinet and up to four stalls that can deliver up to 600 kW to a single EV. Each stall can have two ports, and the system can dynamically allocate power to each vehicle to make the best use of the available power.

Sources indicate that what makes the firm's dispensers different from most competitors is the use of silicon carbide components, which lower energy losses and, subsequently, the amount of money EV drivers have to pay for a top-up. According to Alpitronic, SiC modules enable 97.5% efficiency and allow for smaller, quieter, and cooler stalls.

Alpitronic’s newly introduced factory in Fort Mill, South Carolina, is scheduled to go online in February 2027.

Breaking: Social Media Design on Trial

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • Robbennolt, Alice Curtis Campbell Professor of Law and Professor of Psychology, University of Illinois College of Law.
  • It has been revealed that thousands of lawsuits against social media companies brought by individuals, school districts, and other government entities are making their way through the courts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

By Jennifer K. Robbennolt, Alice Curtis Campbell Professor of Law and Professor of Psychology, University of Illinois College of Law.

It has been revealed that thousands of lawsuits against social media companies brought by individuals, school districts, and other government entities are making their way through the courts. The cases generally allege that the companies caused harm to youth by designing their social media platforms to foster compulsive use and failing to adequately warn users about the potential harms of their platforms.

The first of these cases brought by an individual plaintiff was decided by a jury in March 2026—a bellwether case that will inform decision-making in future cases (K. G. M. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.). The plaintiff, identified by her initials, K.G.M., claimed that Meta and Google had used the “engineering of addiction” to design their apps in ways that encouraged consumers, particularly young users, to remain on the platforms for extended periods. K.G.M. claimed that she began using social media compulsively as a child and that this problematic social media use contributed to depression, anxiety, self-harm, and damage to her relationships. A jury agreed and awarded her $6 million in compensatory and punitive damages. Social media companies ByteDance (TikTok) and Snap (Snapchat) are also defendants in the broader set of lawsuits, but each settled with K.G.M. before her case went to trial.

In a recent development, historically, efforts to hold social media companies liable for harms associated with their platforms have faced a significant legal obstacle: Section 230 of the 1996 Communications Decency Act shields tech companies from liability for harms caused by user-generated content. In this case, however, the legal claims were based not on the content posted on the platforms but rather on the platform design. The lawsuit focused on design features such as infinite scrolling, video autoplay, variable reinforcement, constant push notifications, and beauty filters. K.G.M.’s lawyer likened these features to a “digital casino” designed to keep customers on the social media platforms, arguing that adolescents are particularly vulnerable to their effects.

One challenging aspect of this litigation is establishing a causal relationship between the alleged negligence—the platforms’ design choices—and the mental health harms claimed by plaintiffs. To be successful, a plaintiff must show both that a platform’s design feature can contribute to adverse mental health outcomes and that it did so in the plaintiff’s individual case. The social media companies argue that adolescent mental health is complex and question whether any particular mental health outcome can be causally linked to the design of a social media platform.

Reports from APA (Health Advisory on Social Media Use in Adolescence, 2023) and the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (Galea, S., et al. [Eds.], Social Media and Adolescent Health, 2024) note that this causation question is complex. Psychological studies have found that social media is associated with a variety of negative effects, including anxiety, depression, and attention problems. Yet social media is ubiquitous, and links between mental health and social media use are likely bidirectional, complicating causal conclusions. In addition, individual differences make some customers more susceptible than others to the relevant design features and to developing patterns of problematic use. Research also highlights that social media can have positive effects on mental health, including healthy socialization and self-expression.

Research that more precisely identifies the effects of specific design features on mental health outcomes and examines how individual differences might moderate those effects will be critical in informing the ongoing litigation and any other regulatory or voluntary reforms. Longitudinal, experimental, and quasi-experimental studies will be particularly important in determining which features give rise to problematic use, under what conditions, and for which young people.

Edited by Ashley M. Votruba, J.D., Ph.D., SPSSI Blog Editor, Associate Professor, University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

Industry observers note that turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

It has been revealed that when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious newly introduced female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

Recent findings suggest that photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Big Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a new partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

Industry observers note that as this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a new partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season upgrade not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

Industry observers note that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the latest year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

In a recent development, battlefield Studios confirmed a host of latest changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an problem that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Sources indicate that some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect fresh maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after taking delivery of its first Orange EV e-Triever electric yard tractor in 2024, NSSL saw the electric light. The firm has been moving quickly to transition its yard tractor fleet to zero emissions, and its efforts haven’t gone unnoticed: NSSL is now being recognized by the 2026 Canadian Clean Fleet Awards.

Toronto’s National Shunt Service, Ltd. (NSSL) added its first electric terminal truck to its trailer-moving operations back in 2024 – and they were impressed enough to quickly start buying more, putting their Orange e-Triever and Husk-e trucks to work at customers’ warehouses, distribution centers, and factories. The company has 42 electric trucks working at a number of sites in Canada (up from 27 in June), with looks to have 50 by the end of Q1 2027.

“(Electric is) part of every customer conversation we’re having today,” says Darren Fitzgerald, NSSL’s chief commercial officer. “If customers aren’t asking about electrification, we are bringing it to the conversation.”.

The organization’s commitment to decarbonization recently made them a 2026 Canadian Clean Fleets Award winner, recognizing their growing role in normalizing battery-electric, zero-emission commercial trucks across Canada.

NSSL used Geotab telematics to track pertinent data of each vehicle, giving what Fitzgerald called, “an essential overview of the entire fleet,” that enabled the company to compare efficiencies and cost, as well as the ability to plan ahead.

“The data allows us to identify potential maintenance complications before they result in an outage,” he explains. “Just as importantly, it gives us the analytics to understand idle time, fuel and energy consumption, utilization, and overall operating efficiency.”.

If NSSL’s experience is anything like many, many, many others, they’ll find that the case for electrification is stronger than ever.

#63819. Latest Update: Never Before in the History of Motoring: How the Splendor and Madness Of the Aughts Shaped Today’s Car World

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1356 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Roadandtrack ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Never Before in the History of Motoring: How the Splendor and Madness Of the Aughts Shaped Today’s Car World

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1356 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it was a perfect moment.
  • This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.
  • It felt like driving a Michigan-made Millennium Falcon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it was a perfect moment. In the driver’s seat of a 2005 Ford GT, with my best pal riding shotgun, I stared through the windshield with eyes opened as wide as the car’s headlights. The year was 2007. We were on a stretch of I-80 that dives down the eastern slopes of the Sierra Nevada mountains, from California into Nevada. The early-­morning sun hung low on the horizon in front of us. Looking out on the desert, we saw miles of empty highway, with visibility so sharp that we would see any highway patrol vehicle in our path.

This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

It felt like driving a Michigan-made Millennium Falcon. This Ford could hit 200 mph and beat the Ferrari Challenge Stradale around a road course. It was shamelessly retro, trading hard on the Le Mans pedigree of its GT40 ancestor, but it was also fresh age and American as all hell. It felt unprecedented.

Looking back now, almost 20 years later, I can see that the word unprecedented applied to the whole decade. The Aughts, defined as the years 2000 to 2009, were packed with never-before events and spectacular vehicles such as the Ford GT. It was a time of excitement and optimism, when cars were cool and quicker than ever—until it all crashed into a ditch with the economic downturn. The era was to the car industry what the Sixties were to music, politics, and assassinations. An era of profound change. Of tremendous upheaval. Of darkness and light. Of death and rebirth.

It was the decade that shaped our here and now.

It has been revealed that on the most macro level, the Aughts were when the global automotive ecosphere began ­reordering itself into what we know today. In 2008, ­Toyota overtook GM to become the world’s largest automaker, selling 8.97 million vehicles around the world that year. The ­DaimlerChrysler partner­ship shattered. General Motors, one of the largest corporations on earth, and Chrysler, another of Detroit’s Significant Three, went bankrupt at the end of the decade, and if not for the federal government handing out bags of cash to bail out those legendary companies, they might no longer exist.

GM’s Oldsmobile and Pontiac, two brands that collectively had made cars for nearly 200 years, disappeared during the Aughts. (To be fair, Pontiac did make it a few days into the newly introduced decade, ending production on January 4, 2010, with a last-gasp G6 sedan.) Plymouth also went bye-bye. Saturn assembled its final vehicle in 2009.

The Aughts were also the start of credible alternatives to internal-combustion motoring’s hegemony. The Toyota Prius arrived in the United States in July 2000, then became a cultural lightning rod when sales of the second-­generation model exploded in response to surging gas prices. Hybrid, a term that often applied to a kind of cannabis at the time, suddenly became lingo referring to a kind of car. At the same time, there were inklings of a lithium-ion automotive future. Tesla put out its first battery-powered car, the Roadster, in 2008, and early adopters felt the shock of a 0–60 thrust without the jolt of gears changing. Cars began to morph from machinery into the rolling computer devices that we drive today, as screens proliferated on dashboards and our phones learned to talk to our vehicles. Digital technology wormed its way deeper into every aspect of motoring, a trend that continues, albeit with far less idealism now.

According to recent reports, the decade was a history-defining time in motorsport as well. Globally, racing saw the dawn of a new dynastic epoch. Michael Schumacher, driving for Ferrari, claimed the Formula 1 world championship from 2000 to 2005. In large part, F1 has been a series defined by dynasties ever since. Audi and Tom Kristensen ruled Le Mans for nearly the entire decade, and for the first time, a turbo­diesel won: the R10 in 2006. In NASCAR, Jimmie Johnson took the Cup Series title five years in a row with Chevrolet starting in 2006.

Dynasties on this level of dominance had never happened before in any of these series. I remember sitting in a press conference after the Italian Grand Prix in 2006, when Schumacher (having just won the race) announced his first retirement. The moment he unleashed the news, he teared up and an explosion of camera flashes came from the press corps. The feeling in the room was unforgettable. What Schumacher had done during his career to that point was unprecedented.

It has been revealed that even pop culture had an auto­motive renaissance. The Fast and the Furious premiered on June 18, 2001, with three sequels in multiplexes before the decade was over. F&F grew into Universal Studios’ biggest film franchise and remains the most successful car-movie series ever. Pixar’s Cars came out in 2006 and became Paul Newman’s highest-grossing film, even though viewers never saw his face. Talladega Nights (also 2006) may not invite many critical superlatives, but it unapologetically roasted NASCAR, which was in on the joke. It also popularized the saying, “If you ain’t first, you’re last.” Michael Bay’s Transformers films filled theaters. There was even a Dukes of Hazzard movie with Jessica Simpson playing Daisy Duke, Burt Reynolds as Boss Hogg, and a badass General Lee Dodge Charger. Car video games saw surging popularity, sales, and advancements in graphics. The Aughts gave us Forza Motorsport, plus latest and series-defining installments of Gran Turismo and Grand Theft Auto.

So much was happening in the car world that being a fan felt electrifying. The Camaro, the Charger, and the Challenger were back, and the Mustang was reborn in retro style. The first Cars & Coffee events happened in Southern California, and soon small towns around the U.S. were hosting them.

When you throw all of this together, it made for an earth-shattering decade. Despite the dizzying news cycle, however, it was the cars themselves that we remember most. The Aughts ushered in a new era for halo cars, when automakers set out to build masterpieces that created new expectations for performance and technology. Some would say the Seventies, Eighties, and Nineties were halcyon days for car fans. But the new sheetmetal that graced our roads in the first decade of the new millennium was incomparable.

It has been revealed that ford came up with the aforementioned GT, which was the first real Ford customer supercar made in any significant numbers. Porsche gave us the Carrera GT, a mid-engine rocket ship that is one of the greatest sports cars of all time. Bugatti chased even bigger numbers with the Veyron, the first road car that could crack 250 mph and produce 1000 hp.

Sources indicate that there were plenty of other highlights as soaring corporate confidence and unheard-of development budgets ushered in the arrival of still more icons. This was the decade of the C6 Corvette Z06 and ZR1, the Audi R8, the Ferrari Enzo, and the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren. The Bentley Continental GT and the Porsche 911 GT3 RS debuted, along with the U.S.-eligible Nissan GT-R. V-8 engines were squeezed into the BMW M3, the Cadillac CTS-V, and the Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG. It was a time of heroes.

These cars didn’t just thrill us; they were so unique and outstanding that they redefined the identities of the brands that made them and even motoring itself. That is the true legacy of the Aughts. Even if you’re too young to have lived through those years, you are reaping the rewards today. Because of all of that innovation and ambition, the future through our windshields still looks bright. But maybe a little less bright than it did back then.

A.J. Baime is the author of seven books, including Go Like Hell: Ford, Ferrari, and Their Battle for Speed and Glory at Le Mans, and The Accidental President: Harry S. Truman and the Four Months that Changed the World. An R&T editor-at-large, he has driven cars on racetracks all over the U.S. and Europe, going back to 2007. He is proudly the R&T staff’s slowest track driver.

How Kelly Rowland Keeps Her Eczema Flare-Ups Under Control During Winter

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight.
  • Sources indicate that that’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s.
  • “[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight. But for those with eczema, this time of year can wreak havoc on their skin, too.

Sources indicate that that’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s. During the winter months, she often dreads the cold.

“[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.

Cold weather and indoor heating can reduce humidity, drying out the skin and triggering or worsening eczema flare-ups.

“[What we know] about the skin barrier is that it really is like a gate or wall against the outside world,” Camille Howard-Verovic, MD, a dermatologist at Active Dermatology, told Healthline.

Recent findings suggest that in healthy skin, the barrier controls what enters and leaves the skin. However, for people with eczema, Howard-Verovic remarked they have skin barrier dysfunction, which allows substances such as allergens and irritants to penetrate the skin.

Cold weather can increase transepidermal water loss, a process in which moisture escapes through the skin’s outer barrier and evaporates into the surrounding air.

According to recent reports, “People with eczema have a tremendous amount of transepidermal water loss, so you’re just drier,” said Howard-Verovic. “[You’re] not holding onto the water as well, so that causes the itching and the rash that we feel when we have eczema.”.

Rowland first noticed eczema flares behind her ears as well as on her elbows, arms, and the back of her knees.

“[It] looked like a rash, so that’s what I thought it was all this time, and I dealt with it for so long until after I had my son and then it started to get worse on my face,” she mentioned.

She eventually went to a dermatologist who diagnosed her with moderate-to-severe eczema, a chronic inflammatory skin condition that can cause intense itching, painful skin cracking, thickened skin, and redness or swelling.

When Rowland learned that eczema can be genetic, it made sense to her.

“I remember seeing big rashes on [my mom’s] neck and her arms…so she had it, and I guess I was the lucky one,” said Rowland.

At first, she tried eliminating foods that she thought might be triggers. She also bathed in oatmeal.

In a recent development, “[I] literally have had a tub full of oatmeal, like literally went to the store to get store-bought fresh oats,” she remarked. “I tried everything, and it doesn’t help until you go talk to a doctor about it.”.

At first, she tried prescription topical medications but found them cumbersome.

“I don’t have the time, if I’m being honest, and we live in a world that is moving so fast…I started buying like three tubes of whatever it was I was using and losing it; it was just too much for me,” Rowland said.

Rowland remarked she found relief with Ebglyss, a prescription injectable medication for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. She has also partnered with Eli Lilly and Firm, its manufacturer, to raise awareness about eczema.

Rowland remarked she’s sharing her experience to help others living with eczema, including people she’s met who have experienced greater challenges managing the condition.

“One lady was telling me about how she’s having a tough time [looking] in the mirror cause she doesn’t know who’s looking back at her, and she saw her skin before eczema and after,” noted Rowland.

When she first had symptoms, she noted she felt embarrassed, too.

“[Because] it was just in the middle of my arm space and…[if I] put out my hand to shake someone’s hand, you don’t know if somebody’s judgy,” she said.

Rowland hopes being open about her condition will encourage others to advocate for themselves and talk with their doctor about treatment options.

Because eczema can look different on deeper skin tones, Howard-Verovic noted that a dermatologist can help make the correct diagnosis.

According to recent reports, “Some people may not even know that they have eczema,” she said. “We know that eczema is a rash; it can appear red on certain skin tones, and it can be grey or white on certain skin tones, so it can look a little different.”.

In addition to medication, Rowland said managing stress helps reduce her eczema flare-ups.

It has been revealed that “Before [when] I went on tour, because I was under so much stress, it flared up like crazy, like you wouldn’t believe,” she noted. “We were in the back trying to figure out how to cover certain things up, and we figured some of it out, and some of it was really tricky, but what helped was when I actually just calmed down…not that it helped overnight, but it did just kind of bring the flare down.”.

She said red light therapy, feeling grounded outside without her shoes on, getting vitamin D from natural sunlight, and cooking are ways she reduces ongoing stress.

Industry observers note that “Cooking calms me when my kids aren’t here, and I have a really good [Zen] playlist on,” said Rowland. “[If] you ask me a question [in those moments], I might give you my heart; I’m just so happy.”.

She also tries to cut back on sugar, which she believes triggers flares.

Another way to reduce flares, according to Howard-Verovic, is to avoid hot showers, especially in the winter.

“[We] know eczematous skin likes lukewarm water,” she remarked.

Because Howard-Verovic and her daughter both live with eczema, she set a rule about when it’s time to get out of the shower.

Industry observers note that “[If] you see condensation on the bathroom mirror, you’ve spent too much time in the shower,” said Howard-Verovic. “[That] really hot, hot water feels really good in that moment…but when you get out all that water evaporates, and there’s no moisture in the atmosphere, and it dries your skin out, and now your skin is unhappy again.”.

If you prefer to take baths, she noted use gentle cleansers.

“[There] are bleach baths for really, really bad flare-ups,” she noted.

Diluted bleach baths are sometimes recommended for people with eczema, but they should only be used according to a healthcare professional’s instructions.

Sources indicate that as soon as you get out of the shower or bath, Howard-Verovic noted to apply a quality moisturizer to your damp skin. According to the National Eczema Association (NEA), lotions containing the following ingredients can help ease dry skin associated with eczema.

To help identify appropriate products, look for ones that have the NEA’s Seal of Acceptance.

But a new paper from an international group of scientists working with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) Collaboration, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, takes a stab at closing that gap by identifying 450 cosmic sources in the 20–200 MeV range, providing the clearest view of low-energy gamma rays ever.

#63816. How 'Innocent Parties' Can Navigate Family Estrangement

How 'Innocent Parties' Can Navigate Family Estrangement

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • Industry observers note that the holidays are upon us, and with them comes the annual anxiety over family encounters.
  • According to recent reports, we go through it every year, and I can say candidly, as a therapist, it doesn’t get a lot easier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

Industry observers note that the holidays are upon us, and with them comes the annual anxiety over family encounters. The messaging we receive is all about traditions, togetherness, and reunions, whereas many families experience grief, loneliness, and more due to estrangement within those families.

According to recent reports, we go through it every year, and I can say candidly, as a therapist, it doesn’t get a lot easier. But whereas most of the articles and advice columns we read address the family members experiencing the friction—the son who won’t reconcile with his father, the sister who can’t forgive her brother—there are a lot of people gravely affected by the estrangement even though they do not actively take part in it.

These are estrangement’s forgotten people.

It has been revealed that when two or more relatives cut off contact, the people caught in the middle often absorb the emotional fallout. They get pulled into triangulation in different ways, depending on the specifics of the family dynamics and situation.

Sources indicate that one of my clients, John, experiences this triangulation every year at the holidays. His mother and sister haven’t spoken to each other in years, having fallen out due to the sister’s choice of husband. John loves and is in close communication with both, and this works—more or less—during the year; but the holidays bring greater expectations of “togetherness,” and he feels forced to make decisions, none of which are satisfying to him. Does he choose one holiday party over the other? Manage somehow to rush from one to the other to make both parties happy? Eschew celebrations with both of them?

According to recent reports, his mother and sister pull him into their dynamic by each pressuring John to prove his loyalty to each of them by attending their gathering. When he does, he feels forced to take sides, as each of them used the time to vent about the other. When he refuses to engage in this negative talk, there’s fallout from that, too.

Sources indicate that other families handle the triangulation differently. Rebecca’s large extended family has effectively shunned her cousin Peter after he came out as gay. But while they’ve cut off direct communication with him, they still expect Rebecca to act as the go-between, wanting to make sure Peter gets all their news and, again, passing on subtle negative messages to Peter through Rebecca.

Sources indicate that no one isn’t affected by estrangement, and families often seek to keep tabs on the “missing” relative or relatives. It can be as blatant as, “Where is Dad spending Thanksgiving?” or as subtle as, “Have you talked to your sister recently?” My client Ellen claims this kind of questioning makes her feel like she has to edit everything she says, so that she doesn’t open doors to becoming the conduit, and so that she doesn’t accidentally betray any trust the missing family member has placed in her. Not exactly a jolly family gathering.

And the result is that the family member who is absent from the dinner table gets as much airtime as everybody else.

It helps to remind yourself that you’re not the one who chose the estrangement, and you don’t have to be the stand-in family member. But as we all know, that knowledge isn’t going to make everything all right. Chances are, your people-pleasing tendencies get fired up now, and your choices need to be balanced with what you need and want, and how you want your own family to experience the holidays.

Sources indicate that it may help to name the boundary you’re setting. “Remember, I spent last Thanksgiving with you, and I’m planning on going to Jason’s house this year. Maybe we can get together sometime next week to share leftovers.”.

Sources indicate that this may not have been the message your family of origin gave you, but it’s true for you now: You get to decide. You can set the boundaries you need, and you can reflect them calmly to family members who don’t want to honor them.

For example, you might say to the information-seeking family member, “You're both important to me, so I don't want to talk about either of you with the other. Now, tell me about what you did this week.".

According to recent reports, pausing before answering can also be a great tool. When someone catches you off-guard with a comment or question about a missing family member, taking a breath may help you to not immediately try to smooth things over.

Some mental-health practitioners encourage non-contact between family members who have fallen out over an event or a belief. That’s a topic for a different article, but I have to say that as a family therapist who works to improve communication, I’m optimistic that challenges within families are reparable to a point where agreeing to disagree and coming up with boundaries and limits can be incorporated into the family system and members can be in contact.

In a recent development, the invisible family members do not—and in fact should not—have to be the vehicles for reconciliation, but staying hopeful that it could happen will ease some of your feelings of frustration and resentment. Always staying open to that possibility can help you cope.

The best thing you can do for yourself in these situations is to get in the habit of establishing and maintaining the boundaries you choose and not succumbing to curiosity or hostility in the moment.

For those of us who want everybody to just get along—that’s good. Encourage your family members to meet with a mediator or therapist. It isn’t your job.

And always remember that it’s perfectly reasonable for you to have a close relationship on your own with each party and enjoy them for who they are.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, said in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • In a recent development, the 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy latest names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

“Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, said in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

In a recent development, the 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her newly introduced name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

Collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

Sources indicate that “We see these whales and their families grow each year,” said Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

On Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium announced that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

However, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.
