📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Also, the electric mobility startup spun off from Rivian, is facing another logistics headache. After delaying deliveries of its futuristic TM-B e-bike, the startup has paused shipments entirely to address some software problems that may lead to problematic charging behavior and phantom battery drain.

In an email sent to reservation holders, the firm apologized for the delay, saying it has identified a few software-based complications that are impacting some bikes, and that it wants to address the issues before resuming shipments, as first reported by The Verge. A firmware update is in the works, and Also estimates that deliveries will resume in approximately two weeks, with another update scheduled for November 24.

This is the latest setback for the mobility spinoff that made headlines last year with its software-heavy bicycles and four-wheeled quads. The TM-B e-bike was originally scheduled to be shipped in the spring of this year, but customers started receiving their orders months later, leading to a barrage of negative comments on the Also subreddit. This prompted Saul Leiken, the startup’s product manager, to post a 661-word apology letter, in which he attributed the setbacks to strict quality standards and “significant supply chain challenges.”.

In a recent development, an Also e-bike customer who received his e-bike posted a YouTube video showing how the TM-B behaves when the state of charge gets low, and how the battery drains while the bike is not in use. Aaron Draczyski mentioned he charged his bike in the garage up to 70%, but the state of charge went down to 30% in 24 hours without any usage. What’s more, when the battery level became critically low, the bike refused to charge, throwing an error message that claimed the battery was not installed, even though it hadn’t been removed.

Recent findings suggest that the Also TM-B is unlike most e-bikes out there. Designed from the ground up as a futuristic mobility vehicle, its pedals are not physically connected to the rear wheels. Instead, the rider spins a generator, which provides power to the battery and the electric motor that turns the rear wheel via a rubber belt.

The battery can be recharged via a USB-C port, there’s a round touchscreen to control all of the bike’s features, and the rider can also use a smartphone app to keep tabs on the bike remotely.

The base Also TM-B starts at $3,500, but the Launch Edition models, which have yet to be shipped, cost $4,500. Earlier this year, when the startup declared the first delays, it threw in one of its Alpha Wave helmets and a $250 credit to spend on accessories.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major upgrade. Version 3.8 was the major highlight, of course, with the newly introduced release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

It has been revealed that alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also unveiled that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

Industry observers note that this final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

Industry observers note that the new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

Sources indicate that the Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

Industry observers note that while The Dahlia is the only newly introduced character appearing in this final Amphoreus enhancement, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Recent findings suggest that something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

It has been revealed that chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate initiative, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

An EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

Recent findings suggest that not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

The Gift of Gratitude

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1439 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • Certain times of the year or milestone moments can increase the frequency with which we turn to appreciating the good, though this practice actually has value every single day of the year.
  • In a recent development, the positive psychology movement has helped individuals focus more on what is strong rather than only on what is wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

Certain times of the year or milestone moments can increase the frequency with which we turn to appreciating the good, though this practice actually has value every single day of the year.

In a recent development, the positive psychology movement has helped individuals focus more on what is strong rather than only on what is wrong. As a therapist who works with individuals at various life stages and in situations of distress, I know and embrace the fact that we can’t ignore the overwhelming symptoms, heartache, trauma, and pain; however, I also believe that every individual has strengths and reserves of resilience that deserve to be incorporated and highlighted.

Some people find this practice of being thankful and looking for gratitude moments to be relatively easy, but others find this much more difficult and unnatural.

Several tips are offered here for consideration to build the gratitude muscle.

Like the recent movement to incorporate more bloom-scrolling rather than just doom-scrolling on our phones, the notion of being on the lookout for more positivity can turn out to be a welcome shift for many. We know the gloom and doom exist, and we have plenty of opportunities to focus on it, but also actively seeking out more of the positive, the good, and the upbeat can be incredibly beneficial. Rather than dismissing the negative news or ignoring the overwhelming, we are making room for balance in our bodies and brains.

We can be in charge of our media meal proposal and how we choose to budget our time and attention.

The idea of being on the lookout for gratitude moments is sometimes mistaken for waiting for those “major-ticket” items in life, like a windfall of money, a long-awaited vacation, or a promotion at work. While momentous moments are terrific, they tend to be rarer. However, the small moments of appreciating a delicious meal, a story about an everyday hero, a more scenic route home, the feel of a favorite blanket, or a beautiful bird on a branch are available to us on a much more regular basis.

There is a Japanese concept of Ma, which translates to the gap, interval, or space between things. This is often referenced in Japanese architecture, art, or conversation, but the notion of embracing space or pause can also be utilized in this pursuit of the positive. The gap or interval is not empty or useless; instead, it represents a meaningful void full of potential. So even in those moments between hearing difficult news, awaiting dreaded test results, or anticipating the next migraine headache, we can attempt to orient to something small, quiet, amusing, or pleasant for which we can feel grateful.

We can absolutely embrace the significant, but we might as well also be on the lookout for the small because they are much more plentiful, readily available, and repeatable.

Being aware of possible triggers in our environment can have value and usefulness, but orienting toward noticing the glimmers internally and externally is often underutilized.

According to recent reports, glimmers are those small moments of calm or joy that can cue safety and relaxation for the nervous system. The notion of looking for glimmers was introduced by Deb Dana and based on work by Stephen Porges1, and this practice cues the body toward a state of safety and grounding rather than the fight-flight-freeze mode of response that is activated under threat.

Even on really bad days (or maybe even especially on really bad days), we can choose to notice some good or gratifying things.

Glimmers are the opposite of triggers; both exist in our world, and we deserve to be able to know how to be alert to both.

In a recent development, when we are actively looking for more positive, joyful, beautiful, interesting, or unique in our daily world, we begin to see more of it. Sometimes that elegant, sturdy tree, beautifully colored house, smell of our favorite beverage, or sparkling ray of sunlight coming through the window at a certain time of day has gone unnoticed until we take the time to notice. And once we notice, we tend to orient to seeing it again and again—along with that more satisfying sense of appreciation on repeat.

Orienting to some good news, a funny joke, the stuffy nose that finally cleared up, an enthusiastic pet greeting, or a beloved song on the playlist can all be wonderful in the moment, but what really allows the biggest benefit is to allow the positivity to fully soak in. Like attending to a spill on the counter, dipping a sponge into the corner of the spill for just a moment won’t be as effective as slowly, carefully moving the sponge around the spill to fully absorb the liquid.

Recent findings suggest that when we pause to fully notice the benefits, orient the multi-sensorial delights, and stay with it for several moments, we are more wholeheartedly allowing the affirmative and encouraging to register in our systems. And if we choose to later repeat this positive moment in a journal or in a recounting to someone else, the benefits multiply and the positivity is reinforced.

Recent findings suggest that intentionally, mindfully staying aware of the positive is a happiness hack. And savoring the moment can be a superpower.

Various research studies support the notion that optimistic, grateful people are happier, calmer, more empathetic, less stressed, have better physical health, and even live longer2. Neuroimaging results (MRI and fMRI) also show that practicing gratitude engages key brain regions involved in reward processing and emotional regulation3. These findings support the incredible connection between mind and body.

Studied gratitude interventions include gratitude journals, gratitude letters or texts, and other methods of counting more blessings than burdens. Although there are various self-administered psychological interventions that can improve overall well-being (such as spending time in nature, mindfulness, or acts of kindness), psychological science does consistently show that gratitude practices improve overall mental and physical health.

Recent findings suggest that even if this skill of looking for gratitude, positivity, and thankfulness doesn’t come easily or naturally to you, strive to refrain from self-blame about this. People have a wide variety of circumstances that can influence their ability to orient toward the good, and some of this is influenced by such things as external life circumstances and even genetics. The negativity bias in human brains is also well established and did have an evolutionary benefit4, but times are different now. A broader, more balanced perspective can help. And because brains are neuroplastic, practice in these skills makes for more permanence with these skills.

Be on the lookout for the lovely, and you, too, can optimize your inner optimist.

#63806. Fresh electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Fresh electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results.
  • Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.
  • It has been revealed that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s users were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

It has been revealed that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team says that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

Recent findings suggest that the shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

According to recent reports, researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

The potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

Sources indicate that scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

Finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

Those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team says more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-new, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

For the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s upcoming NTE240E is different, representing a organization’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

According to recent reports, let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so big a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

It has been revealed that plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s newly introduced dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

The combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

Sources indicate that that efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL indicates each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

Recent findings suggest that what’s more, because the big BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the newly introduced NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

  • Industry observers note that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a upcoming revision. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the newly introduced patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Industry observers note that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Recent findings suggest that easily the most interesting change in this enhancement is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a substantial pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

In a recent development, some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

It has been revealed that 1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy complications with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

It has been revealed that something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an upgrade. BF Studios indicates there are still some instances where that might happen, but the problem should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

Letter from the Editor-in-Chief: What a Missed Deadline Taught Me About Switching Off

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I missed a deadline last week.
  • The main problem was I simply ran out of time to write the piece.
  • The other problem and consequence was that I carried a chunk of guilt into the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I missed a deadline last week. The piece you’re reading was supposed to be filed before I headed out on a long weekend to Italy for my wife’s birthday.

The main problem was I simply ran out of time to write the piece. An urgent stakeholder ask out of the blue, a couple of unanticipated work fire drills, and a long-standing evening social commitment earlier in the week made for a perfect storm, and something had to give.

The other problem and consequence was that I carried a chunk of guilt into the break.

It caught up with me at 6 am on the first morning, when I found myself drafting this column in my head. I should have been dozing peacefully. I continued to ruminate on my lengthy to-do list at work deep into day one as we headed from Venice into the Dolomites. My body was in Italy, but my brain was clearly still at my desk.

According to recent reports, switching off, particularly from work, is hard for most of us, and especially in an age of ubiquitous screens and wall-to-wall information competing for our attention. For me, that always-on reality plays a major role in the difficulties I have disconnecting from the daily grind.

I’m fortunate to love my job, and if I’m candid, I probably take a little too much of my identity from it. I hold on tight, and the phone in my pocket is an ever-present enabler.

A meme that has stuck with me over the years goes something along the lines of being an adult is staring at medium screens all day only to come home and stare at a little screen while a big screen is on in the background. The irony is not lost on me that I came across this rather withering take on modern life while scrolling on said little screen.

Industry observers note that regardless of the role the screen plays, psychologists who study employee well-being describe what I was missing for the early part of the weekend as “psychological detachment.” A state where you are genuinely able to not think about work while away from it. The science suggests it’s an key thing to work on.

A 2025 meta-analysis of 32 studies found that vacationing has a strong effect on well-being, and that the effect lasts longer than earlier research suggested. A second, smaller analysis of eight studies points to detaching from work, along with physical activity, as among the most helpful things to do while you’re off. In another study that tracked teachers during a two-week break, exhaustion, anxiety, and low mood all declined, while those who kept ruminating about work recovered less.

Whatever the science indicates, I know that for me the act of stepping away from work and being disciplined about not checking back in while I’m away is critical for my mental health and for staving off burnout. Getting out in nature and hiking or cycling or swimming keeps me present. It resets and recharges my batteries, and it tops up my creativity in a way that I find benefits what I am then able to bring back to the office.

According to recent reports, sure enough, as we drove deeper into the mountains on a crisp, blue-sky day, I could feel the golden autumnal hues and majestic rock formations drawing me in, closer to an elemental feeling of calm and happiness. That sense of equilibrium stayed with me all weekend, and while I’d be lying if I said my mind didn’t occasionally drift to my desk, it was fleeting, with the knowledge that all the things would be waiting for me when I got back. Just like this piece was.

Sources indicate that with Thanksgiving on the horizon, and the holidays coming thick and fast thereafter, I’ll leave you with this bit of hard-earned advice: if your job is deeply entwined with your life and part of who you are, as mine is, time away can sometimes feel like a small act of disloyalty. It isn’t. In fact, it’s probably the most important thing you can do to remain faithful to your work ethic, and to yourself.

And if you’ll be working over the holidays, or you’re not working right now, or you don’t have the benefit of someone on hand to carry some of the load for you (shout out to all the Grannies out there), or your vacation looks very different from mine, that’s all okay. Find the pockets where and when you can: an evening, a walk, an hour in front of a screen, or better yet a book, and let work wait. Above all else, be kind to yourself. That’s how you really give yourself a break.

Robin Hough is the Editor-in-Chief of Healthline, and in addition to this regular Letter from the Editor column, he can be found every other Wednesday in our Healthline Wellness Wire newsletter.

Nearly 1 In 5 Tesla Model Ys Failed Their First German Inspection

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (627 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty quickly.
  • Germany’s TÜV analyzed 9.7 million mandatory roadworthiness inspections carried out between July 2025 and June 2026.
  • Industry observers note that the Model Y finished last out of 109 models for the second year running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty quickly. After reading what German inspectors found underneath some surprisingly young Model Ys, I’d want to know how the suspension was holding up, too.

Germany’s TÜV analyzed 9.7 million mandatory roadworthiness inspections carried out between July 2025 and June 2026. The most revealing comparison was among cars coming in for their first check, at around three years old. EVs won three of the six vehicle classes, but they also occupied the bottom three spots in the overall ranking.

Industry observers note that the Model Y finished last out of 109 models for the second year running. Inspectors found major defects on 18.5% of the Model Ys they checked, up from 17.3% a year earlier and nearly triple the 6.4% average for cars that age. No model in that age group recorded a worse result since the 2015 report. Meanwhile, just 3% of Mazda MX-30 EVs failed, good enough for third overall behind the Mazda CX-60 and Mercedes-Benz GLA.

For the Model Y, inspectors flagged worn suspension joints 24 times as often as they did on comparable cars. They also found defective brake discs on 3.4% of Model Ys, against a 1% average for the age group. Front lighting drew more complaints than usual, too.

Sources indicate that tesla Model Ys covered more miles than average, though. By the time they showed up for inspection, the Model Ys had traveled an average of 36,000 miles (58,000 kilometers). The average car in the group had driven 29,200 miles (47,000 km), and the average MX-30 had covered only 16,200 miles (26,000 km). Those Teslas had driven more than twice as far as the Mazdas in roughly the same amount of time.

The MG4 is the first car from a Chinese automaker to appear in the report, and it finished second from the bottom, with a 16% failure rate despite averaging only 23,000 miles (37,000 km). Inspectors flagged brake discs on 10.3% of MG4s, about ten times the average. Suspension defects were also unusually common. Just ahead of the MG was Tesla’s Model 3, with a 12.5% failure rate at an average of 34,200 miles (55,000 km).

The Model Y’s poor performance in Germany runs counter to its reputation for reliability. American buyers may remember that Consumer Reports ranked the Model Y as its most reliable upcoming EV, though that’s based on owners reporting the problems they’d encountered.

It has been revealed that technical inspections, on the other hand, may find play in a suspension joint that the driver hasn’t noticed. There’s also a difference between buying fresh and buying used, even in Consumer Reports’ own data. Tesla finished last as a brand in its separate survey of five- to ten-year-old cars, which is perhaps more telling.

The German results apply to the Model Y that preceded the Juniper refresh. When I drove the updated Model Y, the softer suspension and newly introduced frequency-selective dampers made it noticeably more comfortable. Whether this softer suspension setup holds up better is something we’ll learn as those cars cover more miles.

Amazon just dropped hundreds and hundreds of deals, and we’ve pulled out some of the best personal audio picks for New Release Fridays and Monday movie nights. Whether you’re looking to spin vinyl, run your personal best, work on some tracks, or just chill, we’ve got something for everyone on this list. Amazon indicates the full Black Friday sale runs through November 30, and our selections highlight the best in wireless headphones, earbuds, IEMs, turntables, portable Bluetooth speakers, soundbars, and whole-home connected setups, among other products. From our top recommendation below through everything that follows, you’ll find premium brands including Sony, Bose, Bowers & Wilkins, JBL, WiiM, Denon, Nothing, Sonos, Marshall, and many more.

Sony’s flagship noise-cancelling headphones are a frequent traveler’s best friend.

It has been revealed that if you’re shopping for a flagship, the WH-1000XM6 is the pair to grab whether you fly, commute, or work somewhere loud. Sony’s QN3 processor drives the noise cancellation, and the earcups fold again, so the headphones pack smaller than the XM5 ever did. In our first impressions, they fixed the last generation’s biggest flaw and sounded better doing it.

Bose’s everyday noise-canceling headphones offer great features for less than a flagship.

It has been revealed that the QuietComfort Headphones are the pair to recommend to anyone who wants excellent noise cancellation without paying flagship prices. You can switch between Quiet and Aware modes or build a custom mode in the Bose app, and multipoint Bluetooth keeps them connected to a phone and a laptop at the same time. Bose rates the battery at 24 hours, and the included audio cable means you can still plug into a seatback screen on a flight.

According to recent reports, if you live in Apple’s ecosystem, the Beats Studio Pro drop to $139.95 (was $299.99) and add lossless USB-C audio for wired listening. For a simpler pair, the Marshall Major V on-ears are down to $79.99 (was $129.99), and Marshall rates their battery at more than 100 hours. You’ll also find options from some of our favorite brands, including Sony, Sennheiser, and Bowers & Wilkins.

Industry observers note that the Nothing Ear (3) earbuds hit $99 (was $149) and bring hybrid noise cancellation and app-based EQ to the mid-price tier. Runners and cyclists who need to hear traffic should look at the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, which leave your ear canals open for situational awareness while you sweat and at the moment only cost $119.95 (was $199.95). See our guide to the best earbuds for more help picking a pair.

The beyerdynamic DT 770 Pro has been a fixture in recording studios since the mid-1980s, and it works just as well for everyday listening at home. The closed-back design keeps outside noise out and your music in, while the plush velour pads stay comfortable through long sessions. The 80-ohm version runs fine from a laptop or phone, though one of the DACs below will give it more headroom, making them a great buy at $139.99.

The beyerdynamic DT 990 Pro is the open-back sibling of the DT 770 Pro above, and it drops to $139.99 (was $199.99). Its wide, airy soundstage suits mixing and critical listening, though the 250-ohm version really wants a dedicated headphone amp. On the in-ear side, the 7Hz x Crinacle Zero:2 remain one of the best ways to hear what wired IEMs can do for about $21. Our list of the best mixing headphones can give you more studio insight.

The WiiM Ultra adds Wi-Fi streaming, a touchscreen, and an ESS DAC to any stereo, and it drops to $296.65 (was $349). For headphones, the Fosi Audio K7 desktop DAC and amp is just $169.98 (was $199.99), and it’s a sensible first upgrade for anyone moving past a laptop’s headphone jack. Those are just a couple of components available to build a better listening station.

A rugged, floating Bluetooth speaker for under $100.

It has been revealed that the Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen.) is small enough to clip to a backpack and tough enough to survive a drop in the lake, since it carries an IP67 rating and floats. Bose kept the 12-hour battery from the original and added AAC and aptX Adaptive support, so both iPhone and Android owners get a better Bluetooth connection than the first model’s SBC-only setup. A customizable shortcut button handles tasks like pairing a second speaker. At $99, it grabs your attention for more than sonic reasons. And for more picks, see our guide to the best portable Bluetooth speakers.

It has been revealed that alternately, the Marshall Emberton III is a palm-sized powerhouse at $89.99 (was $179.99), and its amp-inspired design is rated IP67 against dust and water. For a bigger sound at a backyard party, the Sony ULT Field 5 falls to $188 (was $349.99) … and the bigger, punchier ULT Tower 5 is $299. Those are just two of the two dozen amazing options listed below.

A one-button turntable that plays nice with Bluetooth speakers and real stereos.

Recent findings suggest that the PS-LX3BT is an easy first step up from a suitcase record player. Press play, and it lowers the tonearm, finds the groove, and returns the arm when the side ends, so you never have to cue the record by hand. A switchable built-in phono preamp lets it connect to powered speakers or an amp without extra gear, and aptX Adaptive Bluetooth sends your records to wireless headphones or speakers. At $238, it’s well under the cap on our list of the best turntables under $500.

Recent findings suggest that if the PS-LX3BT above leaves you wanting more, the Sony PS-LX5BT is Sony’s step-up model with more premium components but still a nice price at $398 (was $499.99). Pair either turntable with the Klipsch R-41M bookshelf speakers at $134.47 (was $199) and an amp from the section above for a complete starter system (Klipsch is just one solid option for turntable speakers).

Want to go digital? There are a ton of smart, whole-home, streaming-friendly connected speakers on sale below. We love a compact listening station.

In a recent development, the Sonos Arc Ultra drops to $849 (was $1,099) and delivers Dolby Atmos from a single bar that also anchors a whole-home Sonos system. For a smaller TV or a tighter budget, the Bose TV Speaker is $199 (was $279) and is built to make dialogue easier to follow than a TV’s built-in speakers.

Do you ever find yourself yearning for the feeling you got the first time you drove the Mk 1 Volkswagen Rabbit? The diminutive VW helped usher the hot-hatch segment into the United States. Volkswagen can’t very well sell you a Mk 1 Rabbit any longer, so instead, the firm unveiled a limited-production Rabbit Edition for the 2027 Golf GTI lineup.

Sources indicate that specifically, the Rabbit Edition is arriving for the 2027-½ model year as a sort of midyear update to the GTI lineup. The special edition will slot between the S and the SE in the GTI’s roster and will come with a handful of performance upgrades generally limited to the Autobahn trim. The Rabbit version adds DCC adaptive damping, rides on 19-inch wheels, and wears a set of summer tires, rather than the all-season tires that generally come with the S.

See all results for new 2027 Volkswagen Golf GTI for sale near 23917.

In a recent development, as far as cosmetic changes go, the special edition opts for a blacked-out logo design over the Dark Moss Green Metallic paint, which includes a set of front and rear badges that VW pulled from the Golf R Black Edition’s parts bin. The logos are joined by a black grille, black headlight elements (which are typically red), black wheels, black mirror caps, and a black roof. The one badge that isn’t black is the chrome Rabbit badge on the rear, which serves as an homage to the original.

The Rabbit Edition will be limited to the United States when it goes on sale in the second quarter of next year. Exact pricing hasn’t been announced, but the Rabbit should cost somewhere between the $36,230 starting price of the S and the $40,420 starting price of the SE.

Latest Update: Why Being Home for the Holidays Makes You Feel 15 Again

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (845 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • It has been revealed that every year, my clients tell me some version of the same story.
  • Industry observers note that this topic frequently comes up in my sessions during the holiday season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

It has been revealed that every year, my clients tell me some version of the same story. I've been making so much progress, but after five minutes at my parents' house, it all goes out the window.

Industry observers note that this topic frequently comes up in my sessions during the holiday season. They've spent months learning to better manage their emotions, or set healthier boundaries, and they’re enjoying the benefits of that work in their day-to-day lives.

In a recent development, then, when they go home for the holidays, they automatically fall back into old habits. They're arguing with their siblings like teenagers, getting defensive when their parents offer unsolicited advice, and agreeing to things they don't want to do just to keep the peace.

Does slipping back into familiar family dynamics mean you haven't actually changed? That underneath all that growth, you're still the same person you were at 17?

It has been revealed that long story short, the answer is “no.” Sliding into old roles is a completely normal, well-documented phenomenon in personality science. Let’s talk about why this happens—and what to do about it.

Personality traits are a descriptive summary of how you typically think and behave. Do you generally experience significant emotions or are you less reactive? Do you usually initiative ahead or fly by the seat of your pants? Are you typically the person driving the conversation, or do you often find yourself hanging back to observe during social situations?

Importantly, personality is not black and white. Even though we often think about personality traits as categories (e.g., introvert vs. extrovert), traits actually exist on a continuum. People can fall anywhere along that spectrum (e.g., always introverted, often introverted, 50/50 depending on the situation, often extraverted, always extraverted).

Where you fall on a particular personality trait reflects how you tend to think, feel, and behave on average, across different situations. For example, you might be more extraverted when you're out with friends and much quieter in a work meeting.

You can shift that average, making it more likely that you'll think, feel, and behave in ways that align with your values. But even as your personality shifts, some situations will still bring out more or less of a particular trait. In other words, if you've become generally more confident and even-keeled in your everyday life, a few days of feeling insecure or emotionally reactive around your family doesn't mean you've lost the progress you've made.

And those personality averages do shift across our lives. Research shows that, on average, people become more emotionally stable, more conscientious, and better able to get along with others as they age.

Much of this personality change takes place between ages 20 and 40, a period when many people leave their family homes and gain greater freedom to choose who they spend time with and how they spend their days.

It has been revealed that these new environments can encourage different patterns of behavior. Maybe growing up, you learned that raising your voice was the only way to get your point across. But in your adult friendships and romantic relationships, communicating calmly may be much more effective. As these healthier ways of interacting are reinforced over time, you may gradually become a more agreeable person.

Sources indicate that even if you've changed considerably over the years, your family may expect you to behave like your old self, and those expectations may pull you to fall back into old habits. For example, if you grew up trying to keep the peace by sacrificing your needs, you might find yourself agreeing to sleep in a separate room from your partner to appease your parents, even if you’ve been actively making progress toward being more assertive.

Industry observers note that and the stress of the holidays doesn't help. When we're tired or otherwise stretched thin, we're more likely to fall back on well-practiced responses. The behaviors your family pulls from you were learned early and reinforced repeatedly, so under stress, your brain dusts them off because they require less energy than the newer patterns you might be working on.

The good news is that being around your family gives you an opportunity to practice the new ways of thinking and behaving you’ve been working on. Think of it like playing a video game on hard mode: The skills are the same, but the challenges are tougher. You can't necessarily change how your family treats you, but you can make small changes in how you respond to them. And over time, those small changes can help create a different dynamic. Here are three ways to start:.

If you want to start showing up differently, The Personality Action Plan helps you identify one specific action that could make the biggest difference in changing an old pattern and create a plan to put it into practice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

Industry observers note that “We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”.

Sources indicate that last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that showed intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a new approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

“Fiona was such a gift,” said Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

Sources indicate that fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s EV push in America has skewed practical, for the most part. The ID.4 was a generic crossover, so close to an electric take on the Tiguan that VW is actually rebranding it as the ID. Tiguan. And the ID. Buzz, whimsical styling aside, is an electric van—a very expensive electric van. But VW has not abandoned its small, fun hatchback roots in Europe, and the German brand is continuing the celebration of the 50th anniversary of its GTI sub-brand with an EV: the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, which it will debut at the Essen Motorshow later this month.

In a recent development, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is an all-electric, track-ready, front-wheel drive hot hatch. VW shoehorned an electric drive system intended for larger RWD vehicles into the sub-compact ID. Polo GTI; that gives the concept outputs of 362 horsepower (up to 389 hp in short bursts) and 406 pound-feet of torque, a massive increase from the 223 hp and 214 lb-ft in the standard model.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can hit a top speed of 149 mph, and it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds—quicker than a Golf GTI but not quite as quick as a gas-powered Golf R—with the launch control engaged.

This VW’s body is heavily modified from the standard model, as well. It features a two-door layout instead of four, flared fenders, and an enormous front splitter, diffuser, and rear wing. VW also stripped out the interior for track work by deleting the rear seat and cargo area. The two front seats are Recaro racing bucket seats with five-point harnesses, and the interior also has an integrated Tornado Red roll bar.

Sadly, this is just a concept for now. Volkswagen has not committed to building an ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, and even if the brand did, it would be unlikely to be offered in the American market. VW did reveal a very cool ID. GTI concept back in 2023, which it has claimed will be more fun than the combustion-powered GTIs. And Volkswagen, pointedly, has not ruled out bringing that car to America—though getting the pricing and timing right in the U.S., with an unstable tariff situation and variable EV incentive climate, may prove tricky.

#63794. Why the Most Politically Savvy Colleague Gets Things Done

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1095 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Why the Most Politically Savvy Colleague Gets Things Done

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • In a recent development, A project lead needs budget for a project.
  • So in the week before the meeting, she has three separate conversations with people who will make or break the decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

In a recent development, A project lead needs budget for a project. She knows the formal process: Write the proposal, present it at the monthly meeting, and then wait for feedback. She also knows how decisions are actually made in her organization.

So in the week before the meeting, she has three separate conversations with people who will make or break the decision. First, she talks with the finance director, who worries about cost overruns at the end of every quarter. Then, she talks with the operations head, whose team always gets dragged into projects that sometimes go nowhere. Next, she talks to the program lead who will "volunteer" to manage the project.

Industry observers note that by the time she presents, the decision has effectively been made. People raise issues briefly as a formality because they already feel assured, and some even answer their own questions because they like the solution they were shown in advance.

Sources indicate that there are a couple of ways to look at this approach. It's definitely an effective approach. Some people would call it clever, but not everyone would mean that as a compliment.

Sources indicate that the resourceful style is one of the "dark side" personality styles: everyday patterns that can help or hinder us at work, depending on how strongly they show up and in what form. Its most extreme form resembles what psychologists call Machiavellianism, a cynical, self-serving approach to other people.

People who do this as a regular course of action share this way of viewing the world, navigating work through relationships—many of them transactional. They understand how power structures and networks truly exist in reality, separate from the official org chart or chain of command. They swiftly pick up on who makes decisions, or who suggests the ideas that get picked up more often than not.

They tend to be strategic, focused on outcomes, and can be very adaptable when the route to a goal changes or latest obstacles emerge.

Researchers have studied the useful side of this for decades under the name "political skill." Ferris and colleagues (2005) developed a measure of it with four parts: social astuteness (reading people and situations), interpersonal influence, networking ability, and apparent sincerity (coming across as genuine).

Recent findings suggest that A meta-analysis by Munyon and colleagues (2015) found that political skill was linked to higher productivity, career success, a better reputation, and greater job satisfaction. It predicted task performance even after accounting for broad personality traits and general intelligence.

Sources indicate that when the researchers looked at the four aspects separately, networking, influence, and apparent sincerity predicted performance. Social astuteness on its own did not. Reading the room is a useful start, but the rarer skill is reading a room and influencing your place in it.

Industry observers note that at their best, resourceful people do exactly that. They get around obstacles that stall everyone else, and find the person who can make a decision or make the obstacles go away. They can get other people to support them to make unpopular decisions, and if they get the desired results, some people will respect and admire them for it.

Sources indicate that this can be done proactively and prosocially, or in ways that are counterproductive and manipulative. Organizations and even small teams are political whether or not anyone likes it, and someone who can find ways of making things work is necessary for any high-functioning team.

Sources indicate that the dark side emerges when people become collateral damage. Consider a colleague who builds trust with a peer during a brutal restructuring, learns that the peer is burned out and looking for another job, and later uses that confidence to edge them out of a key role when budgets tighten.

As I discussed in a post on destructive behavior in the remote office, a manipulative person can work this way with surgical precision, especially when much of the work happens across different and poorly organized communication channels.

However, it is possible to operate in some gray areas while still maintaining respectful and mutually beneficial relationships. Arguably, it's a more successful strategy in the longer term.

The research on Machiavellianism shows the cost of being too ruthless. A meta-analysis by O'Boyle and colleagues (2012) found it was linked to more counterproductive work behavior, meaning behavior that harms colleagues or the organization. Its link to lower job performance was small and inconsistent, which fits the idea that this style can deliver short-term results while eroding the reliability and trust that long-term work requires.

In a recent development, it helps to compare this style with more combative, rule-breaking tendencies that are compulsive instead of calculated. Combative people tend to push boundaries, take visible risks, and ask forgiveness rather than permission. Resourceful people usually leave the rules intact and work the system instead. They do not need to skip the approval process when they have already lined up the approvers.

It has been revealed that that can make the resourceful style harder to spot, and its destructive form harder to challenge. Nothing improper has technically happened. The damage is a loss of trust amongst teams.

As I argued in "The Surprising Upside of Your Dark Side," the question to ask of personality styles is: How do you use them?

Industry observers note that people who read power well will always have an advantage in certain types of work. Whether others experience them as a valuable ally or a threat depends less on how well they play the game than on what they are trying to accomplish.

Ferris, G. R., Treadway, D. C., Kolodinsky, R. W., Hochwarter, W. A., Kacmar, C. J., Douglas, C., & Frink, D. D. (2005). Development and validation of the Political Skill Inventory. Journal of Management, 31(1), 126–152. https://doi.org/10.1177/0149206304271386.

According to recent reports, macRae, I. (2022). Dark social: Understanding the darker side of work, personality and social media. Bloomsbury.

In a recent development, munyon, T. P., Summers, J. K., Thompson, K. M., & Ferris, G. R. (2015). Political skill and work outcomes: A theoretical extension, meta-analytic investigation, and agenda for the future. Personnel Psychology, 68(1), 143–184. https://doi.org/10.1111/peps.12066.

O'Boyle, E. H., Jr., Forsyth, D. R., Banks, G. C., & McDaniel, M. A. (2012). A meta-analysis of the Dark Triad and work behavior: A social exchange perspective. Journal of Applied Psychology, 97(3), 557–579. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0025679.

  • Industry observers note that americans bought an estimated 48,678 used EVs in October, according to the latest EV Market Monitor from Cox Automotive.
  • It has been revealed that cox says used EV sales rose 4.7% from September to October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that september was a good month to be selling a used Tesla Model Y. Sales jumped nearly 14% from August, and the Ford Mustang Mach-E did even better. The Chevrolet Equinox EV beat both, though, with a nearly 42% increase. A month later, only one of those three electric crossovers was still gaining buyers: the Chevy.

Industry observers note that americans bought an estimated 48,678 used EVs in October, according to the latest EV Market Monitor from Cox Automotive. That’s up 4.7% from September and 73.2% year over year. Used Tesla sales, meanwhile, fell 5.4% from September, with the Model 3, Model Y, and Model X losing ground.

It has been revealed that cox says used EV sales rose 4.7% from September to October. However, its September report put sales at 47,862 vehicles. October’s total of 48,678 is 816 higher, which is a 1.7% gain; Cox doesn’t explain the discrepancy.

Tesla still dominated the used EV scene, though. The change was one spot down, with Chevrolet moving ahead of Ford into second place. Hyundai and BMW rounded out the top five. The Equinox EV and Blazer EV added to their September gains, while the Kia EV6, Nissan Leaf and Volkswagen ID.4 also found more buyers than in the previous month.

Cox states this is because a growing supply of cars coming off lease is giving shoppers more choices across brands and price points.

That 73% jump over last year deserves a little context. October 2025 was the first full month after the federal EV tax credit ended and Americans bought about 30,000 used EVs. In March, sales hit a record of nearly 43,000. EVs made up 3.3% of U.S. used car sales in October, matching September’s record and up from 2% a year earlier.

Sources indicate that for used EV shoppers, the more useful number might be $36,582. That was the average asking price for a used EV in October, down from $36,767 in September and 1.9% below a year earlier. The Equinox EV, ID.4, Mach-E and Nissan Ariya all got cheaper.

It has been revealed that used Teslas didn’t for a second consecutive month, rising 1.8% to an average of $34,109. Even after that increase, the average used Tesla was listed for about $2,500 less than the average used EV.

Sources indicate that used EVs still carried a $2,236 premium over gas cars and hybrids, up slightly from $2,137 in September. Dealers had 38 days’ worth of used EVs on hand at October’s sales pace, versus 47 days for gas cars and hybrids.

According to recent reports, at October’s sales pace, traditional dealers had enough used Teslas to last 32 days, the shortest supply of any major brand Cox tracked. Cox’s count leaves out Tesla’s own stores. Another study looked at how long each used EV spent on dealer lots in September. The Audi Q4 E-Tron Sportback sold the fastest, and no Tesla made the top ten.

Over on the new-car side, Americans bought 83,262 EVs in October, down 3.9% from September but up 3% from a year earlier, marking the first year-over-year gain of 2026. EVs’ share of new sales slipped from 6.5% in September to 6.2% last month. The average buyer paid $56,221 for a new EV, even with incentives averaging $6,375 per vehicle. Dealers had 85 days’ supply of new EVs, more than double their used inventory.

October wasn’t all bad for Tesla. While sales of second-hand Model Ys fell, Americans bought 36,366 brand-upcoming examples, up 9.4% from September. It accounted for nearly 44% of all new EVs sold in the country.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hailey Bieber is sharing her experience with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a condition she says has fueled her growing interest in women’s health research.

The Rhode Beauty founder recently confirmed a $5 million, three-year partnership with the Foundation for Women’s Health in an interview with Women’s Wear Daily (WWD).

“As a woman, I feel frustrated by the lack of research, the lack of awareness, the lack of certain conversation around it,” Bieber told WWD.

Motherhood has also shaped her perspective. Bieber welcomed her son, Jack Blues, with her husband, Justin Bieber, in 2024, describing the experience as a “really intense and special journey.”.

She also shared that she “struggled” with PMDD after giving birth, noting that there’s “not a lot of conversation or research around it.”.

“When we can identify with each other and have conversations relating to each other and talking about the things we’re dealing with and struggling with, I do think it makes it feel like less of a lonely journey,” Bieber stated.

PMDD is a complexcondition that causes severe physical and psychological symptoms that typically occur in the days or weeks leading up to menstruation.

“What distinguishes PMDD from the more common PMS (premenstrual syndrome) is the severity of the symptoms and how significantly they can interfere with daily functioning,” Sari Eitches, MD, dual board certified physician and medical advisor to Terra Mare, told Healthline.

“Another defining feature is the timing: symptoms typically worsen in the week or two before a period, resolve within a few days after menstruation begins, and are minimal or absent during the rest of the cycle,” she noted.

Eitches also noted that PMDD is a chronic condition that can affect women at any stage of their reproductive lives, from adolescence through perimenopause, as long as they are having menstrual cycles.

“It is caused by a sensitivity to cyclic hormonal and neurotransmitter fluctuations, so [it] can occur in anyone with a menstrual cycle, though stages of hormonal fluctuation- including postpartum, weaning breastfeeding, and perimenopause- can be a trigger,” she added.

According to research published in 2024, approximately 1.6% of women and girls meet the strict diagnostic criteria for PMDD, equivalent to an estimated 31 million people worldwide.

A higher percentage of 3.2% have a provisional diagnosis, meaning a healthcare professional may believe a person has PMDD, but symptoms have not been measured for a sustained amount of time to meet the criteria for a confirmed diagnosis.

Eitches mentioned that women with a personal or family history of depression or anxiety may be more prone to developing PMDD, as are women with a family history of PMDD itself.

“PMDD is understood to be caused by a combination of heritable biological sensitivities and environmental triggers. These can include a history of trauma, chronic stress, and other chronic medical conditions,” she noted.

Eitches also mentioned that you should consider seeing a doctor if your symptoms are severe enough that they’re interfering with your ability to go to work or school, maintain your relationships, or participate in your life in the same way that you do during the other weeks of the month.

According to recent reports, to diagnose PMDD, a healthcare professional will review your medical history and symptoms and may perform a physical exam. They will typically ask you to track your symptoms over at least two menstrual cycles.

A PMDD diagnosis generally requires at least five symptoms, including at least one mood-related symptom, that occur before menstruation, improve shortly after a period begins, and significantly interfere with daily life.

Treatment options for PMDD include prescription medications and over-the-counter treatments that may help relieve certain symptoms, such as:.

Eitches noted that cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can also help manage symptoms.

Lifestyle changes may also help manage PMDD symptoms, including practicing relaxation techniques, eating a balanced diet, limiting sugary and salty foods, and getting regular physical activity.

Eitches noted that getting enough high quality sleep and resting on a consistent schedule is also important.

“I also recommend focusing on a whole-foods-based diet, limiting added sugar and caffeine, and avoiding cigarette smoking,” she stated.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, most mid-cycle refreshes touch only the surface stuff: a upcoming grille, new headlights, new wheel designs. They typically don’t venture too far into the mechanicals. Toyota flipped the script in its approach to the 2027 Sienna hybrid minivan, mostly leaving the visuals alone and focusing instead on the substantive bits. The result is a minivan that’s more upgraded than it looks.

It has been revealed that much like a person who is very bad at seeing those magic-eye illusions, you could stare at a picture of the 2027 Sienna all day and nothing fresh would make itself apparent. The exterior is unchanged, although one paint color (Cypress) has been dropped in favor of a new hue (Storm Cloud). The trims have also been rejiggered: The Limited is gone, and the XSE picks up some of its features and becomes the new penultimate trim beneath Platinum. Otherwise, every inch of mid-cycle-refresh effort went into the underlying tech and the powertrain.

See all results for used cars for sale near 77002.

Sources indicate that the base LE loses its 8.0-inch infotainment screen as Toyota democratizes digital real estate, granting every Sienna a 12.3-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch gauge display. New LED cabin lighting arrives, and the rear-seat entertainment picks up major upgrades with native apps and a new touchscreen. The sound-deadening material behind the dashboard has also been tweaked.

Sources indicate that we saved the best bits for last. The 2027 Sienna adopts Toyota’s latest (sixth-gen) hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the Lexus ES. The old nickel-metal hydride battery is replaced by a lithium-ion pack that stores more energy, and it feeds a redesigned and more efficient electric motor to produce a combined 251 horsepower—six more than its predecessor. All-wheel-drive models energize the rear axle with an additional motor, though that doesn’t raise output any. Toyota estimates a 7.5-second run to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive guise, rising to 7.6 with all-wheel drive (since there’s more mass and no extra oomph). Either way, that’s 0.3 to 0.4 second quicker than the 2026 Sienna. Our long-term 2021 Toyota Sienna Limited AWD did the deed in 7.6 seconds.

According to recent reports, the 2026 Sienna earned EPA fuel-economy estimates of 36 city, 36 highway, and 36 combined for front-wheel-drive models and 35/36/35 for all-wheel-drive variants. While official numbers have not yet been released for the 2027 model, Toyota claims city improvements of 3 mpg (FWD) and 4 mpg (AWD), with combined estimates rising between 1 and 2 mpg.

In a recent development, because these changes might not seem like much on paper, Toyota gave us access to both a 2026 Sienna and a 2027 Sienna to better experience the changes. And we’re glad we had that opportunity, because the revised Sienna does make for a vastly improved driving experience.

See all results for used cars for sale near 77002.

Recent findings suggest that we liked the 2027 Sienna more before we even pushed the start button. The Sienna’s new steering wheel puts switches in more sensible locations; it’s much easier to operate on the fly, plus it looks better. The 2026 model’s tech feels a full step behind the 2027 model’s, with its analog gauge cluster (on the lower trims) and tiny info display, or the complete lack of USB-C ports. Thankfully, with the 2027 Sienna’s new tech comes a whole host of electrical-system changes, including a move to USB-C. Our tangled morass of a cable drawer thanks you, Toyota.

In addition to sprinkling better ports around the cabin, the Sienna’s fresh updated tech also enhances the driving experience. The electronic power steering is lighter at lower road speeds, making around-town navigation slightly less onerous, and it also exhibits better on-center stability at highway speeds, again eliminating some tedium. The brakes also include a feature Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels to reduce body roll in cornering; after taking both Siennas to our 10Best evaluation loop, we can confirm that the revised Sienna does corner ever so slightly flatter, and you don’t even need to drive like a Car and Driver editor to feel the improvement.

As for the Sienna’s powertrain, we loved it in the latest generation of Lexus ES, and we very much enjoy it here as well. As Toyota promised, the sixth-gen hybrid brings noticeable improvements to noise, vibration, and harshness. In the 2026 model, the combustion engine sounds and feels coarser low in the rev range. In the 2027 model, the powertrain is both smoother and quieter, with an audible reduction in cabin noise (a change we’re excited to get the chance to confirm via testing at a later date). Simply put, driving the 2027 Sienna offers a more serene experience—for both driver and passengers—than you’d find in its predecessor.

According to recent reports, some changes incur massive cost penalties, but the 2027 Sienna doesn't ask too much extra off the top. It's estimated to come in around $44,500 for the base LE model with front-wheel drive. For context, the 2026 Sienna started at $42,915 for the base LE, rising to $60,305 for the top-spec Platinum; the slightly more rugged Woodland Edition was $53,695. Given just how much better the 2027 Sienna drives, we think it’s worth the higher cost of entry.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical complications, some of which are a little unusual.
  • Sources indicate that immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some newly introduced holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the enhancement’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical complications, some of which are a little unusual.

Sources indicate that immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The problem is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios promptly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The concern remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer stated it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

It has been revealed that ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to rapidly jump into the latest content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the revision.

According to recent reports, but Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

In a recent development, A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

Recent findings suggest that this is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the latest upgrade has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

Sources indicate that it’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many concerns at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.
